_readme: Capacity, protocol and wire constants -- the single source for both the firmware
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Arduino/libraries/TaskInterpreter/TaskLimits.h was hand-written
in Phase 0 and carried these numbers alone. The compiler was about to become a second
copy, which is how START_LINE_MAX ended up mirrored across two repos with nothing
keeping it in sync, and how baudRate ended up in nine files. Generating both from
here means a limit has exactly one definition.
THE RATIONALE IS THE POINT, NOT DECORATION. Every `rationale` below is emitted into
the generated header as a comment. A generator that dropped it would replace the
best-explained file in the repo with a wall of naked #defines, and the next person to
wonder 'why 64 and not 192' would have to re-run a hardware spike to find out. If a
value changes, its rationale and `measured_by` change with it.
BETTER STILL, these are ANNOUNCED at connect time in the CAP line
(docs/protocol-negotiation.md), so a host/firmware mismatch is DETECTED rather than

_group_rationale: MEASURED, not chosen -- docs/spikes/avr-ram.md. At these limits the table costs
1440 bytes and a real ATmega2560 build leaves 5397 bytes of SRAM free at the worst
instant: peak stack, measured by canary-painting at 777 bytes, coinciding with the
Why 64 and not the ~192 that measurably fits: a limit exists to catch a runaway or
malformed spec before it reaches a box, not to extract the last byte. 64 states is
2.4x the largest target task (seq2_retention compiles to roughly 26 nodes), enough
slack that no legitimate task meets it, while leaving ~5 KB for the interpreter's

TG_MAX_STATES.rationale: 2.4x the largest target task. 8 bytes each.

TG_MAX_EDGES.rationale: Two per state on average; the widest band is the response fan-out. 4 bytes each.

TG_MAX_TIMING.rationale: One entry per distinct duration. The largest current spec declares 17. uint16 each -- see the durations note.

TG_MAX_ACTIONS.rationale: Actuator set/clear operations across all node entries. 2 bytes each.

TG_MAX_TRIAL_TYPES.rationale: Mirrors task_spec.v1.json's own maxItems on contingency.trial_types. 8 bytes each.

TG_MAX_STAGE_ROWS.rationale: Both existing shaping schedules use 5 rows; 8 leaves room without inviting a schedule nobody can reason about. 4 bytes each.

TG_MAX_TIMING_SETS.rationale: Total timing rewrites across every stage row. 4 bytes each -- and note this record is ABSENT from the budget formula published in the spike doc, because the probe never allocated it. The real table is 192 bytes larger than that formula says; headroom is unaffected.

TG_MAX_PORTS.rationale: Response-port rows. 16 bytes each -- the largest record, because a port carries six strobe codes. Sized 8 to match the watch mask's width even though only 7 ports can be watched alongside an engagement channel; a spare row costs 16 bytes and removes an off-by-one between two arrays that are indexed by different things.

TG_MAX_STIMULI.rationale: Stimulus rows, one per emitter a task can present. 4 bytes each. Eight covers the odor manifold's twelve lines minus the ones no current task addresses, and no spec declares more than two.

TG_MAX_WATCH.rationale: Watchable input channels, and therefore the width of TgNode.watchMask. THIS IS A HARD CEILING, not a budget: the mask is a byte, so a ninth channel has no bit and would be silently unwatched. With one engagement channel that leaves 7 response ports, which is what TG504 enforces. It is declared here because it was previously implicit in three places at once -- the struct's watchPin[8], the packer's WATCH_SLOTS, and the rule's help text -- which is the mirroring pattern this file exists to end.

TG_PROTO_VERSION.rationale: Bumped on any breaking wire change. 1 is the legacy bare-START path, which is what an un-migrated box still speaks -- so a host seeing no CAP line at all can assume PROTO=1.

TG_SPEC_VERSION.rationale: schema/task_spec.v1.json. Travels with every compiled table so a recorded session can be reconstructed against the schema that produced it.

TG_VOCAB_VERSION._value_is_a_mirror: DERIVED at codegen time from strobe_vocab's own vocab_version; this literal is a fallback and a reading aid. It was hand-typed until the vocabulary went to 2 and TaskLimits.h stayed at 1 while TgStrobes.h moved -- two headers in one library disagreeing about one number.
TG_VOCAB_VERSION.rationale: schema/strobe_vocab.v1.json. Separate from spec_version because the vocabulary grows (append-only) far more often than the schema changes.

TG_CHANNELS_VERSION._value_is_a_mirror: DERIVED at codegen time from channels.v1.json's channels_version. See TG_VOCAB_VERSION.
TG_CHANNELS_VERSION.rationale: schema/channels.v1.json. Separate again: a box with a different pinout changes this and nothing else. NOTE this tracks what a channel MEANS, not where it is -- the pinout has its own version and does not move this number.

rationale: Chosen as the highest rate that is both adequate and openable by generic POSIX
tools: macOS stty rejects 250000 and above, so screen/minicom/cu cannot reach
them, and losing 'screen /dev/cu.usbmodem... <rate>' as a 2 a.m. debugging path is
a poor trade for headroom the measurements show is unobservable.
The +2.12% divisor error at 16 MHz is harmless HERE because it is symmetric: the
2560 and the 16U2 bridge are both 16 MHz AVRs computing the same UBRR, so they
agree exactly, and the USB side is packet-based. A 300-strobe integrity test on
real hardware confirmed zero loss.
Cable length does not bear on this. The run to the host is USB full-speed
signalling; the UART this governs is centimetres of trace inside the board.
Measured: at 115200 every inter-strobe delta is already a millis() tick boundary,
so a faster wire changes nothing that reaches the record. At 9600 the seventh
strobe in a burst blocks for 10-12 ms. See docs/decisions.md D13.
Mirrors START_LINE_MAX in the firmware repo's BehaviorBox.h. Present so the CAP
line can announce it and the host can stop guessing -- NOT an independent source
of truth while the legacy START path is still live.
The original is checked rather than trusted because the firmware cannot report the
failure: readLineInto() truncates an overlong line and drops the rest, so an
over-declared profile runs the session on whichever values happened to fit.
uint16. Firmware stores timings as signed int (max 32767) AND uses 32767 as the
StageStep 'never' sentinel (BehaviorBox.h:531-536), so a legal duration sits one
step from a magic one. uint16 doubles the range and removes the collision -- a
deliberate, documented divergence from current firmware.
The compiler must REJECT a duration above this rather than wrapping. See
docs/decisions.md D6.
emitStrobe formats "%03d\t%lu" and the host's IN_SESSION parser is
^\d{1,3}\t\d+$, so a 4-digit code is unparseable on the host and silently
dropped. A wire-format limit, not a preference.
Five codes already exceed 255, which is why the compiled table stores strobes as
uint16. See docs/decisions.md D5.

TG_NO_STROBE.rationale: Sentinel for a node that emits nothing -- the omission path, which current firmware leaves deliberately silent (D4). Out of band: above TG_STROBE_MAX, so it can never collide with a real code, unlike the 32767 sentinel it replaces.

_group_rationale: The runtime net the compiler cannot provide. Every node carries a compiled
max_dwell_ms budget, but two of them -- sampling release and consumption --
wait on the SUBJECT rather than on a clock, and no static analysis can bound
them. This is the number used there.
A false trip ends a healthy session; a missing trip leaves a box stopped with
an animal in it, invisibly, looking like an operator stop. Both are bad, but
the fault is strictly better than the hang because it is RECORDED and the
hardware is safed. So the ceiling is set generously and the cost of that is

rationale: MEASURED, against the only unbounded state the corpus can speak to. Across
75,590 recorded sampling releases (ODOR_OFF -> ODOR_UNPOKE): median 290 ms,
p99 2.45 s, p99.9 5.3 s, and a single longest observation of 21.1 s. 30 s is
1.4x the longest dwell ever recorded and 5.7x p99.9.
Consumption (STOP_FLUID -> WATER_UNPOKE) cannot be measured from the corpus:
the firmware that produced it waited for the wrong edge, so those 305 samples
are re-poke latencies and not withdrawals (docs/firmware-changes.md #0). The
ceiling covers it by argument instead -- it is the same animal leaving the
same kind of port, after a reward rather than after an odor, and nothing
suggests it is longer.
30 s also matches lazyDelayMax, the longest DELIBERATE wait anywhere in the
system, so a state that exceeds it is by construction not a normal wait.
Slack added to a node's compiled budget before the watchdog will call it an
overrun. A polling loop legitimately overshoots its duration by up to one poll
interval, and a blocking Serial write can add more, so a HOLD of exactly 500 ms
returning at 503 ms is normal and must not be a fault.
250 ms is ~50x the largest poll interval any spec declares and ~0.8% of the
unbounded ceiling, so it is loose enough that no healthy state trips it and
tight enough that it does not meaningfully widen the window a real hang sits
in. It applies only to nodes WITH a budget; unbounded nodes use the ceiling
directly, which already carries its own margin.
